extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys, and EPO examiners involved in European patent prosecution and opposition
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for examination of European patent applications and patents, covering procedural practice and substantive requirements (formalities, search, examination, opposition, amendments and patentability under the EPC). Intended to be followed by examiners and practitioners during prosecution and opposition before the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the European Patent Convention and Implementing Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines give instructions on the practice and procedure to be followed in the various aspects of the examination of European applications and patents in accordance with the European Patent Convention and its Implementing Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines are intended to be applied in line with the EPC and its Implementing Regulations and have been amended to reflect legal and procedural developments. The March 2022 edition is the official version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination (Part A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part A: Guidelines for Formalities Examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part A outlines the procedures for formalities examination, mainly with regard to grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search matters (Part B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B: Guidelines for Search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B deals with search matters relevant to European patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural aspects of substantive examination (Part C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part C: Guidelines for Procedural Aspects of Substantive Examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part C relates to procedures to be followed in substantive examination proceedings before the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and limitation/revocation procedures (Part D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part D: Guidelines for Opposition and Limitation/Revocation Procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part D relates to procedures to be followed in opposition and related proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: General procedural matters (Part E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part E: Guidelines on General Procedural Matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part E summarizes procedural matters relevant to several or all stages in proceedings before the EPO and contains information about procedure before the EPO as designated or elected Office, applicable to Euro‑PCT applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements other than patentability (Part F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part F defines the requirements which the application must fulfil other than patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F addresses matters such as unity of invention (Art. 82), sufficiency of disclosure (Art. 83), clarity (Art. 84) and the right to priority (Art. 87 to Art. 89).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Art. 82)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention (Art. 82) is a requirement the application must fulfil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described within Part F as one of the non‑patentability requirements to be examined during application processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (Art. 83)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficiency of disclosure (Art. 83) is a requirement the application must fulfil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F covers examination for whether the application discloses the invention sufficiently for a person skilled in the art to carry it out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (Art. 84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity (Art. 84) is a requirement the application must fulfil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F includes guidance on assessing the clarity of claims and description as a formal/substantive requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to priority (Arts. 87–89)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to priority (Art. 87 to Art. 89) is a requirement addressed in Part F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F contains guidance on entitlement to priority and related procedural aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Part G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part G deals with the requirements of patentability provided for in Art. 52 to Art. 57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G covers exclusions from patentability (Art. 52(2) and Art. 53), novelty (Art. 54), inventive step (Art. 56) and industrial application (Art. 57).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from patentability (Art. 52(2) and Art. 53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions from patentability as provided for in Art. 52(2) and Art. 53.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G addresses which subject-matter is excluded from patentability under the EPC (e.g., discoveries, mathematical methods, programs as such, etc., as per Art. 52(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Art. 54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty (Art. 54) is a requirement of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of whether the claimed subject‑matter is new over the prior art is covered in Part G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Art. 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive step (Art. 56) is a requirement of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G provides the EPO's approach to assessing inventive step (non‑obviousness) for European patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application (Art. 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial application (Art. 57) is a requirement of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G includes guidance on whether the claimed invention is capable of industrial application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and corrections requirements (Part H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part H deals with the requirements relating to amendments and corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H focuses on admissibility of amendments, compliance with Articles and Rules governing changes to applications and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of amendments (Rule 80 and Rule 137)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions of admissibility of amendments are governed by Rule 80 and Rule 137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H highlights procedural rules on when and how amendments may be made during various proceedings (e.g., during opposition, examination, or after grant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Article 123(2) and (3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with Art. 123(2) and (3) is required for amendments and corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H addresses prohibition of added subject‑matter (Art. 123(2)) and prohibition of extension of protection after grant (Art. 123(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections (Rule 139 and Rule 140)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections under Rule 139 and Rule 140 are covered in the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H includes guidance on correction of errors in documents (Rule 139) and correction of mistakes in decisions (Rule 140) and the conditions under which such corrections are allowed.
